Part 1: The Executive Competition Dossier

1. Executive Summary & Strategic Positioning

In modern sustainable townships—such as Sime Darby Property’s City of Elmina, Bandar Bukit Raja, and KL East—mechanical equipment operates continuously. From commercial central air-conditioning chillers in community mosques and retail centers to domestic washing machines and stormwater drainage pumps, thousands of rotating electromechanical assets power daily living.

Today, nearly all of this machinery is managed via reactive "run-to-failure" maintenance or arbitrary calendar rounds. When mechanical wear starts:

  • The Parasitic Energy Leech: Unlubricated bearings and fatigued dampers create friction. Modern inverter-driven motors automatically pull 15% to 35% excess electrical wattage to maintain speed, completely undetected by conventional circuit breakers for months.
  • Catastrophic Disruption: Minor RM 25 component degradation cascades into motor burnout or compressor seizure (costing RM 800–RM 1,800+ for appliances, and RM 15,000–RM 50,000+ for commercial chillers).
  • Severe Landfill E-Waste: 70 kg appliances and multi-ton industrial compressors are scrapped into landfills simply because a single consumable wear component failed unnoticed.
The Dual-Engine Strategy: From Dynamic Stress Crucible to Township-Scale Fleet
Apex PdM pairs an extreme-stress physical benchmark (validated on a 1,400 RPM inverter machine) with a turnkey township infrastructure platform. The rotating electromechanical failure physics (vibration harmonics → acoustic friction → parasitic power drag → breakdown) is universal across both home appliances and commercial township chillers.

4. End-to-End System Architecture & Dual-Core Discipline

The platform architecture spans four tightly coupled tiers: Physical Edge Sensing, High-Reliability Dual-Core Firmware, Cloud Streaming Infrastructure, and Machine Learning Prognostics.

4.1 Engineering Rationale: Mastering the Ultimate Dynamic Stress Crucible

To validate multimodal predictive maintenance under peak operational stress rather than simulated lab environments, the Apex architecture was physically built, packaged into an IP65 industrial enclosure, and benchmarked on an active Samsung WW10TP44DSX inverter washing machine:

  • The Ultimate Dynamic Benchmark: A washing machine drum spinning at 1,400 RPM with wet laundry is one of the most mechanically turbulent, violently vibrating, and acoustically noisy rotating systems in existence. If our sub-RM 50 sensor pod can reliably isolate micro-vibrations, acoustic friction, and motor wattage here without triggering false alarms, transitioning this exact sensor pod to stationary commercial HVAC chillers and water pumps in mosques or malls is mechanically simpler, more stable, and an engineered certainty.
  • Field-Verified Real-Time Data Pipeline: The physical rig actively captures, computes, and streams 3-axis kinematics (200 Hz), 24-bit acoustics (16 kHz), and motor wattage (1 Hz) in real time to Google Firebase, validated by over 6,628 verified real operational data points across 10 genuine cycles and continuous feature streams.

Figure 4.2: Assembled Physical Hardware Rig in IP65 Pod

4.2 FreeRTOS Dual-Core Discipline & Hardware Safety Guard

To eliminate thread contention, audio buffer under-runs, or network jitter, our custom C++ firmware enforces strict hardware processor isolation:

  • Core 1 (Real-Time Sensor DSP Engine): Dedicated strictly to continuous 200 Hz MPU-6050 FIFO reading (44 Hz anti-alias filter) and 16 kHz INMP441 I2S DMA buffer acquisition. RMS sound energy is computed in real time using 24-bit bitshift filtering. Thread-safe updates are guarded with portMUX_TYPE spinlocks.
  • Core 0 (Network & Protocol Engine): Handles Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, Tapo P110 local encrypted KLAP queries (1 Hz), HTTPS Firebase uploads, and wireless ArduinoOTA updates.
  • Hardware Force-ON Watchdog Guard: Background watchdog polls smart plug relay state every 1.0s. If accidentally switched off, it immediately re-engages the relay within 1,000ms.

4.3 Edge Telemetry Packaging & Dual-Tier Streaming Protocol

To bridge high-speed physical sensors with cloud analytics without latency or sample loss, the firmware formats telemetry into a standardized, lightweight JSON envelope guarded by spinlocks:

{ "ts": { ".sv": "timestamp" }, "session": "wash_2026-10-16_085721", "ax": -0.12, "ay": 0.35, "az": 9.78, "vibe_mag": 9.82, "audio_rms": 248.5, "state": "RUNNING", "cnt": 1420, "uptime": 142 }
  • Dual-Tier Transmission: Core 0 executes a 1 Hz Hot Path (HTTPS PUT to Firebase /live.json) powering the real-time operator HUD with <1s latency, and a 5.0s Cold Path archiving batches to /sessions/<id>/ for long-term ML training and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) regression.
  • Local Fail-Safe (LAN, HTTP): Serves the latest feature window, the last 2.56 s of raw 200 Hz acceleration and a short raw audio clip (never sent to the cloud) over the local network, and buffers up to 48 windows (about 4 min) while offline for later upload. Local endpoint reachability is not yet verified.

Part 4: Rapid Online Portal Submission Q&A Pack

Q1: Problem Description (160 words)

In modern sustainable townships, electromechanical equipment—from residential washing machines to central air conditioning compressors in community mosques and retail centers—is managed reactively. When bearings, seals, or dampers degrade, they create mechanical friction. Because modern inverter motors automatically draw excess electrical current to maintain speed, degraded machinery leeches 15% to 35% excess electrical power for months without tripping circuit breakers.

Eventually, unaddressed friction leads to total motor burnout or compressor seizure. A minor, unaddressed RM 25 component failure cascades into catastrophic hardware destruction (costing RM 800–RM 1,800+ for appliances and RM 15,000–RM 50,000+ for commercial chillers). This forces premature scrapping of 70 kg domestic machines and heavy commercial castings into landfills. In large developments, manual technician inspections miss early acoustic and kinematic anomalies, leaving township operators blind to mounting energy waste and sudden public service failures.

Q2: Innovation & Uniqueness (180 words)

Apex PdM is the first low-cost (< RM 50 production BOM) multimodal edge-AI platform that fuses four synchronized physical dimensions: high-frequency 3-axis kinematics (±16g @ 200 Hz), ultrasonic/acoustic sound pressure (16 kHz 24-bit I2S DMA), active electrical power (W, V, mA @ 1 Hz), and ground-truth operational phase.

Existing commercial predictive maintenance systems cost thousands of ringgit per sensor, target only heavy industrial oil-and-gas plants, and produce frequent false alarms during normal high-speed operations. Apex solves this via phase-conditioned anomaly modeling: by conditioning vibration and sound against ground-truth operational states, our algorithm distinguishes between high-speed centrifugal dynamics and actual mechanical failure.

Furthermore, our FreeRTOS dual-core firmware architecture isolates 200 Hz sensor sampling from network streaming, ensuring zero dropped audio samples and millisecond-level responsiveness. Combined with our automated Force-ON safety guard, Apex delivers industrial-grade prognostics at a consumer-accessible price point.

Q3: Technical Implementation (185 words)

The physical prototype utilizes an ESP32 dual-core microcontroller running custom C++ FreeRTOS firmware: Core 1 executes uninterrupted 200 Hz MPU-6050 FIFO reading (44 Hz anti-alias filter) and 16 kHz INMP441 digital I2S DMA buffer capture, wrapping data into a standardized JSON telemetry envelope guarded by portMUX_TYPE spinlocks. Core 0 executes dual-tier streaming: a 1 Hz hot path pushing to Google Firebase /live.json for live dashboard rendering, and a 5.0s batch archival path for ML model training, while concurrently polling Tapo P110 active power via encrypted local KLAP protocol. Ground-truth machine state is integrated via Samsung SmartThings REST API.

We overcame three critical technical hurdles: (1) Thread Starvation & Jitter solved by dual-core processor affinity and spinlock memory handoffs; (2) Spin Cycle False Alarms solved by a 45-column ML prognostic contract conditioning vibration thresholds on ground-truth phase; (3) Smart Plug Safety solved by an automated background watchdog that detects accidental relay deactivation within 1,000ms and forces power back ON.

The system is validated by over 6,628 verified real operational data points across 10 genuine cycles + continuous feature streams, and an active live web dashboard deployed at https://washer-pdm.pages.dev.

Q4: Target Audience & Adoption (175 words)

Apex serves two primary user tiers across Sime Darby Property developments: (1) Township Facility Managers (B2B) managing commercial assets across community mosques, suraus, retail malls (e.g., Elmina Lakeside Mall), and clubhouse facilities. Adoption is driven by out-of-the-box retrofitting: non-intrusive clip-on pods attach to existing compressor housings in under 10 minutes without rewiring, feeding directly into a unified township facility dashboard. (2) Township Residents (B2C) in smart residential precincts, reached through native integration with the Sime Darby Township Resident App with intuitive Machine Health Index notifications.

To drive early adoption, Sime Darby Property can bundle Apex sensor pods as a standard smart sustainability amenity in new home handovers, while piloting commercial compressor monitoring across flagship communal buildings to demonstrate immediate utility bill reductions.

Q5: Feasibility & Execution Roadmap (180 words)

We have already completed Phase 1: an extreme-stress physical benchmark on an active 1,400 RPM inverter machine, dual-core FreeRTOS firmware, 6,628+ verified telemetry records across 10 genuine sessions, and a live cloud dashboard deployed on Cloudflare Pages.

Our future execution roadmap comprises three structured phases: (1) Months 1–3 (Township Pilot): Retrofit 25 communal rotating assets in City of Elmina (8 central AC chillers in Masjid Elmina, 11 rooftop compressors at Elmina Lakeside Mall, and 6 clubhouse filtration pumps). (3) Months 7–12 (Township-Wide Scaling): Standardize Apex pods as an optional sustainability add-on for new residential handovers across Bandar Bukit Raja and City of Elmina, establishing an automated circular economy parts-replacement network.
